summary: Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau. He held posts at Renmin University of China (~2007) and Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard University (~1971–1975). His career includes professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University (~2005).

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Jing'an Buddhist Academy and Rissho University (~1969–1975), and under Dongchu and Lingyuan. He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Shenghai Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., and studied with teachers including Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Ram Shankar Tripathi.

Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading and earned a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido (~1981–1986), alongside training with several traditional Buddhist masters.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Önpo Tenzin Norbu, and Mipam Gyatso, among others. He held teaching posts at Shri Singha Shedra, Dzogchen Monastery, and Dzongsar Monastery.

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries under teachers including Gungthang Lodrö Gyatso. He served as president of the Buddhist Association of China and dean at the Buddhist Academy of China.

Sherry B. Ortner (born 1941) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan. She held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and UCLA.
Sherry Chayat (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vassar College and under traditional teacher Eido Shimano (~1975–1998).
Shi Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a BA at the University of Kelaniya and earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2016).
Shi Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Shichang Ma (born 1938) is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in Peking University's Archaeology Department beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a sinologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928) and later held an academic post there (~1949–1968).

Shigeki Moro (born 1972) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and computational fields. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities, studying under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, and held posts at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui (born 1935) is a scholar of Sinology and historical archaeology who studied at Waseda University (~1954–1963) and later served as a professor there (~1980–2006).

Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974), and served on the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).
Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology who served as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999, 2017).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Shigeo Yokoyama (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1981). He held posts at Okayama University (~1988–1999) and Nara Women's University (~1999–2020).

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, later holding posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, and Otani University (1955–1978).
